html:
A loose union of Senegal and the Gambia, formed in February 1982 after Senegalese troops put down the 1981 coup attempt and dissolved in 1989.

Senegal's president Abdou Diouf was its president and Dawda Jawara its vice president. It planned a joint army and a customs and currency union. The Gambia feared being swallowed by its far larger neighbour and its re-export trade, a big part of its economy, depended on its own low tariffs. The plans stalled, and Senegal ended the confederation in 1989. Relations between the two have swung between close and tense since.
sum: A loose union of Senegal and the Gambia, formed in February 1982 after Senegalese troops put down the 1981 coup attempt and dissolved in 1989.
